newsitem.title: CHINA: China '96 edible grain demand seen at 267.6 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China '96 edible grain demand seen at 267.6 mln T.

text.p: China's demand for edible grain is seen hitting 267.6 million tonnes in 1996, the State Grain Reserve Administration said a report seen in Beijing on Sunday.

Annual grain consumption per capita in rural areas, where most of China's people live, was seen at 260 kg while the figure for urban areas was 101 kg, said the State Grain Reserve Administration's Cereal and Feed Information.
Demand for feed grain was forecast at 120 million tonnes in 1996, up 15 percent from the year before, the report said.
Industrial demand for grain, mainly to be used for distilling spirits, was expected to be about 53 million tonnes this year, a rise of 18 percent compared with last year, it said.
China needed an estimated 16.5 million tonnes of seed grain in 1996, it said.
About 13 million tonnes of grain would be lost during storage and transportation, it said.
Grain added to state reserves as well as that lost during transportation and storage would total about 13 million tonnes, it said.
